recipes.title: Keep recoverable versions of personal files
recipes.description: Choose by operating system, interface preference, and where encrypted backup history will be stored.

picks.label: Open-source CLI fit
picks.reason: Encrypted, versioned backups across supported local and remote storage backends.
picks.tradeoff: Requires command-line setup and an independently tested restore process.

picks.label: Linux and Mac desktop fit
picks.reason: Puts Borg profiles, schedules and archive restoration behind a desktop interface.
picks.tradeoff: Depends on Borg compatibility and does not provide native Windows support.

picks.label: Premium desktop fit
picks.reason: Windows and macOS application for encrypted backups to selected local or cloud destinations.
picks.tradeoff: Software licensing and storage-provider charges may be separate.

recipes.title: Prepare a complete PC recovery image
recipes.description: Disk imaging protects an operating-system installation; keep personal-file backups and restore tests as separate requirements.

picks.label: Graphical boot-media fit
picks.reason: Creates and restores disk images through a GUI with Clonezilla image compatibility.
picks.tradeoff: Requires booting recovery media and selecting the destination carefully.

picks.label: Deployment specialist
picks.reason: Provides disk and partition imaging with specialist deployment workflows.
picks.tradeoff: The boot-media workflow and many options require more familiarity.

picks.label: Premium Windows fit
picks.reason: Integrates Windows image backups and rescue-media recovery.
picks.tradeoff: Commercial edition and subscription terms apply.

recipes.title: Choose a recovery tool by failure type
recipes.description: A failing device, lost partition, and missing file metadata need different tools; recover output to separate storage.

picks.label: Read-error imaging
picks.reason: Copies readable areas of damaged media and records a resumable recovery map.
picks.tradeoff: It copies sectors; it does not reconstruct a lost filesystem or undelete files.

picks.label: Lost-partition specialist
picks.reason: Investigates missing partitions and supported damaged filesystem structures.
picks.tradeoff: Repair modes can modify disk metadata; work from an image when practical.

picks.label: Signature-carving fit
picks.reason: Looks for supported file content even when directory metadata is unusable.
picks.tradeoff: Recovered files can lose their original names and folder layout.

picks.label: Advanced graphical recovery
picks.reason: Offers filesystem reconstruction, disk inspection and RAID-related recovery.
picks.tradeoff: Free-edition limits and advanced editing risks require review.

recipes.title: Find what is consuming disk space
recipes.description: Start with measurement and file review before choosing anything to delete.

picks.label: Windows NTFS specialist
picks.reason: Combines a treemap with Windows NTFS metadata scanning.
picks.tradeoff: Commercial use requires the appropriate license; WizTreeMac has different behavior.

picks.label: Open-source Windows fit
picks.reason: Shows a Windows directory-size breakdown and treemap.
picks.tradeoff: A size visualization does not establish whether a file is disposable.

picks.label: Terminal and SSH fit
picks.reason: Provides interactive directory-size navigation without a graphical desktop.
picks.tradeoff: Permissions limit visibility, and live files may change during a scan.

recipes.title: Manage files across several folders
recipes.description: Compare graphical dual-pane workflows with terminal-first navigation.

picks.label: Open-source dual-pane fit
picks.reason: Offers a commander-style graphical interface across supported desktop platforms.
picks.tradeoff: Advanced operations and plugins still have a learning curve.

picks.label: Premium Windows workflow
picks.reason: Offers extensive Windows file-management customization and automation.
picks.tradeoff: Commercial licensing and configuration effort apply.

picks.label: Terminal workflow fit
picks.reason: Combines asynchronous terminal navigation with configurable file previews.
picks.tradeoff: Preview helpers and terminal image support need compatible setup.

recipes.title: Help someone on a remote computer
recipes.description: Match the connection model to the user’s setup and who operates the coordination service.

picks.label: Self-hosting fit
picks.reason: Supports remote desktop and file transfer with optional self-hosted coordination.
picks.tradeoff: Operating a server and unattended-access policy adds administration.

picks.label: Commercial support fit
picks.reason: Provides a cross-platform remote-support workflow with commercial administration options.
picks.tradeoff: Professional use requires the appropriate license.

picks.label: Linux multi-protocol fit
picks.reason: Collects RDP, VNC and SSH connection profiles in one Linux desktop client.
picks.tradeoff: It needs an existing remote server and suitable protocol plugins.

recipes.title: Connect private devices across networks
recipes.description: Mesh networking connects devices; it is distinct from buying an Internet exit VPN service.

picks.label: Managed coordination fit
picks.reason: Automates private WireGuard-based device connectivity with identity and access policies.
picks.tradeoff: Hosted coordination and plan-specific limits apply.

picks.label: Self-hosted coordination fit
picks.reason: Combines peer networking and access controls with a self-hosting path.
picks.tradeoff: Running the management infrastructure adds operational work.

picks.label: Manual tunnel specialist
picks.reason: Supplies focused encrypted tunnels with explicit peer configuration.
picks.tradeoff: Identity management, discovery and routing must be designed separately.

recipes.title: Replace reused passwords with a vault
recipes.description: Choose between a locally controlled database and a hosted synchronization and sharing workflow.

picks.label: Local encrypted vault
picks.reason: Keeps a cross-platform encrypted password database under the user’s control.
picks.tradeoff: Sync, backups and recovery must be arranged deliberately.

picks.label: Hosted sharing fit
picks.reason: Offers cross-platform vault access and a free entry tier with optional paid sharing features.
picks.tradeoff: Advanced account and organization features vary by plan.

picks.label: Premium shared-vault fit
picks.reason: Provides integrated desktop and browser workflows for family and team vaults.
picks.tradeoff: Requires an ongoing subscription and account recovery planning.

recipes.title: Encrypt files before storing or sharing them
recipes.description: Select a file vault, mounted container, or command-line envelope according to how applications access the data.

picks.label: Cloud-folder fit
picks.reason: Encrypts files individually before a supported sync client uploads the vault.
picks.tradeoff: Cloud synchronization conflicts and separate mobile terms still matter.

picks.label: Mounted-container fit
picks.reason: Lets desktop applications use a mounted encrypted volume.
picks.tradeoff: Container synchronization and recovery planning need care.

picks.label: Scripted-file fit
picks.reason: Encrypts file streams for explicit recipients or a passphrase.
picks.tradeoff: Secret keys and recipients are managed outside a graphical vault.

recipes.title: Run another operating system in a virtual machine
recipes.description: Match host architecture, desired guest, and setup complexity.

picks.label: General desktop lab
picks.reason: Provides a cross-platform graphical VM workflow with snapshots and virtual networks.
picks.tradeoff: Guest architecture support and Extension Pack licensing must be checked.

picks.label: Mac emulation fit
picks.reason: Provides a Mac interface to virtualization and architecture emulation.
picks.tradeoff: Acceleration depends on backend and host/guest architecture.

picks.label: Ubuntu CLI fit
picks.reason: Launches Ubuntu virtual machines with optional cloud-init configuration.
picks.tradeoff: Focused on Ubuntu rather than arbitrary guest operating systems.

picks.label: Simple Linux desktop fit
picks.reason: Offers a streamlined GNOME workflow to download and create desktop guests.
picks.tradeoff: Advanced hypervisor controls are less exposed than in virt-manager.

recipes.title: Inspect hardware before changing settings
recipes.description: Separate component identification, disk health indicators, and stress testing.

picks.label: Windows sensor fit
picks.reason: Combines detailed hardware inventory with sensor monitoring and logging.
picks.tradeoff: Sensor availability is hardware-specific and commercial use has separate terms.

picks.label: Linux report fit
picks.reason: Generates hardware and software information reports with optional benchmark tasks.
picks.tradeoff: Synthetic benchmark results need workload context.

picks.label: Storage-health specialist
picks.reason: Reads supported drive health data and self-test logs through smartctl and smartd.
picks.tradeoff: Controllers can hide data, and a passing health check does not guarantee future reliability.

picks.label: Bootable RAM specialist
picks.reason: Exercises supported system memory outside the installed OS.
picks.tradeoff: Requires boot media and cannot rule out every intermittent hardware problem.

recipes.title: Investigate a slow or unstable network
recipes.description: Measure the path, controlled throughput, and per-process usage separately.

picks.label: Interactive path fit
picks.reason: Shows route-level latency and probe statistics in a terminal.
picks.tradeoff: Intermediate routers can rate-limit replies without dropping application traffic.

picks.label: Controlled throughput fit
picks.reason: Measures a configured client/server network workload.
picks.tradeoff: Needs a test process at both endpoints and is not a speed test of every application.

picks.label: Windows per-app control
picks.reason: Tracks per-application traffic and allows bandwidth rules.
picks.tradeoff: Commercial licensing applies and rules can affect application behavior.

picks.label: Linux per-process view
picks.reason: Groups live bandwidth by the responsible process.
picks.tradeoff: Needs capture privileges and is not a long-term accounting database.
